chapter: Small's Paradise, Fletcher Henderson and Horace
title: Brothers who could not get along in bands
summary: Caldwell lists band brothers such as Tommy and Jimmy Dorsey, the White brothers and the McRaes who quarrelled.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Fletcher was the same way. But that brother --

Oh, you know, what he did to Fletcher -- well, of course, his brother's peculiar, you know. Now, take, for instance -- I know three, four different brothers' band, never got along so good, like Tommy and Jimmy. They didn't get along until after their mother got them together after their father died. And she laid the law down to them.
The Tommy and Jimmy thing was a little different, wasn't it? I mean that was like, you know, they'd kind of fight, but it --
No, it wasn't deceitful. LIke the White brothers, Harry White, trombone player, and he had his brother, Harry, trombone, and his cousin. They had a band there, terrific band.
Uh-huh. He come out of Pennsylvania. They had about --
Yes. They were born up therewhere Tommy Dorsey was born.
That's right. That's where they were born. They wasn't too far from where Tommy and Jimmy --
Well, how many White -- were there two White brothers?

There were two White brothers, a lot of cousins played, but now his brother was a very nice French piano player. Never could get along. Like the McRae brothers, they brought a terrific band from Philadelphia years ago.
Brothers -- it's a funny thing about brothers, yeah.
